messages:
dmitri: Heads up — after the 6.3 kernel rollout to the P4 pools in eu-west2 we're seeing multiple hosts fail to attach the NVIDIA module. Affected ~12/120 P4 hosts. Some pods hit cudaInit / NCCL handshake timeouts and we lost ~10% effective GPU capacity. Logs below from one host:

 dmitri: ```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[ 1234.568000] nvidia: probe of 0000:00:03.0 failed with error -110
[ 1234.568100] nvlink: nvlink_probe failed -110
[ 1234.568200] device eth0: rx timeout, disabling queue 0
[ 1234.568300] pod kubelet: cudaInit failed: -110
```

alice: Is this limited to 6.3 kernels? We rolled 6.2 to a subset last week without issue. Did the driver or CUDA package versions change in the AMI?

ben: -110 is a probe timeout. Could be a timing change in module init or PCI rescan ordering. Also seeing "rx timeout" for NICs is suspicious — might be PCI link resets/power management differences in 6.x.

carla: On the orchestration side, NCCL logs show repeated handshake timeouts: `NCCL WARN Call to connect failed (errno 110)`. Affected pods go CrashLoopBackoff trying to init GPU.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-rollout-job (eu-west2-p4-pool) status: paused by infra@dmitri due to probe failures. Canary nodes: 3/3 failed.

 dmitri: Current impact: 12 hosts reporting probe failures, 9 hosts automatically drained by kubelet (gpu plugin failing), ~80 pending OOM-sensitive pods queued for GPU scheduling. We already started evacuating VMs that still come up clean.

 eva: Short-term mitigation options:
- Pause remaining 6.3 rollout (already done).
- Scale up fallback capacity in us-west2/us-east (spin up p4s on 5.15 image) and shift provisioning regionally.
- Attempt manual `modprobe nvidia` on a failed host to see if reload succeeds, but logs show immediate -110.

 ben: I can run a quick bisect between 6.2 and 6.3 config differences (kernel cmdline, CONFIG options). But also we need to repro on a pinned host. Suggest a reproducible test job that runs `modprobe nvidia; dmesg -w --level=err` then loads a small CUDA sample.

 carla: Opening a support ticket with NVIDIA. I'll attach dmesg + `lspci -vvv` + kconfig and kernel cmdline. Noting that net rx timeouts appear in same timeframe as module probe failures — could be PCI atomic context changes.

 alice: I'm going to revert the image in the autoscaling group for the remaining eu-west2 machines to 5.15 and set a temporary hold on kernel-upgrade pipeline for this pool.

 dmitri: Action items:
- alice: pause rollout + revert remaining eu-west2 ASGs to 5.15 (in progress)
- ben: run kernel config diff + repro job, post artifact link here
- carla: NVIDIA support ticket + attach logs (ticket opened: INC-3821)
- eva: provision 10 extra 5.15 p4 hosts in us-west2 and add to scheduling pool to reduce backlog

 ben: Quick note — I ran the repro job on a spare host and saw identical `probe ... -110` when the host was booted with `intel_iommu=on` in the cmdline. Booting same host without IOMMU enabled allowed the module to load. Could be IOMMU interaction regression in 6.x.

 dmitri: Good find. We'll include that in the support ticket. For now rolling back kernels is safest. If anyone hits a host that still has GPUs visible, please avoid scheduling GPU-heavy jobs on them until we finish the patch/rollback.

 carla: NVIDIA support asked for stack traces and a `modprobe --verbose nvidia` trace. I'm uploading to the ticket. Also requested whether anyone saw a change in DKMS/ABI between our driver (510.x) and image packaging.

 eva: Provisioning update — spun up 8 5.15 p4s in us-west2 and started rebalancing pending jobs. Backlog dropped from 80 -> 22 in 18m. Will continue until capacity stable.

 dmitri: We'll keep eu-west2 kernel rollout paused and not resume until we have either a kernel workaround (cmdline/IOMMU tweak) or an NVIDIA driver fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

 alice: TL;DR: pause, revert remaining nodes, move capacity, open vendor ticket, bisect.

 ben: I'll share the bisect script + repro logs in #eng-infra-artifacts when ready.

 carla: Ticket INC-3821 updated with logs and IOMMU note. Nvidia assigned engineer.

 infra-bot: create-ticket: INC-3821 (NVIDIA support).

 dmitri: I'll follow up with a short postmortem if this persists tomorrow. For now owners are assigned.
